notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white EU plates with yellow taxi plates; since mid-2022 a new format shows the coat of arms, and new electric cars have green plates.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black-and-white wedge-shaped bollards with a red reflector at the front and white at the back; blue reflectors are also fairly common.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete poles with thin holes running all the way to the ground are the most common type; wooden poles are also frequent.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are white on red; black-and-white ones are much rarer.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: A very distinctive language with many acute accents, umlauted o's, long words, and Ő and Ű with double acute accents found nowhere else.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Streets end in utca, and bigger roads use út; both words are unique to this language.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green kilometre markers run along most roads; on highways they match small yellow boxes on maps.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Sign posts are often abnormally tall, sometimes taller than the camera.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Signs are fixed to posts with four bolts in a tall rectangle, rare in other eastern countries.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs show five stripes and a figure with a belt worn very low, unique here; a rarer type has four stripes and a bag.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Roads use green signs, and M-prefixed highways blue ones, with the number in a small shield; direction signs match with white inner borders.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Road lines are white, but those on bicycle lanes are typically yellow.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Most generation 3 was shot in winter, so it looks grey and dead; a small grey flag often sits on the antenna.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A black generation 4 car that never shows an antenna, and a rare white one.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Light-painted stone houses with almost always red tiled roofs, mostly single storey in suburbs, old but well kept in centres.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Phone numbers have 8 or 10 digits; the first two (or third and fourth) digits are the area code, except the capital's single 1.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The first digit of numbered roads is ordered in a circle around the capital.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Many town names use local prefixes that hint at the region.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs with a thick metal frame suggest the western part of the country.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue or green arrow-shaped street signs attached to poles or street lights point to the far northeast county.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The southeast is extremely flat; the north and west have forested hills, the tallest mountains being in the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The biggest lake, moderately hilly, built up and full of small hotels, is the only large lake seen on coverage.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Puszta around Hortobágy is barren, wet natural grassland, unlike the mostly cultivated plains.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The road east of Tornanádaska by the border is recognisable by snow, bollards and a railway beside it.
